# InclusivePay

Voice-first, accessibility-first payments for everyone. Say a command, hear it read back, confirm, enter your PIN, and the money moves through the PayPal **sandbox**.

**Stack:** Node/Express · PayPal Payouts, Invoicing and Webhooks · PayPal Server SDK (generated by APIMatic) · an LLM with tool calling (Gemini free tier by default) · AG Grid Community · Web Speech API · Server-Sent Events

## Run it

```bash
npm install
cp .env.example .env     # then put your sandbox credentials in .env
npm start
```

Open **http://localhost:3001** (the server serves the front end, so don't open `index.html` directly). Use Chrome or Edge for voice.

> `.env` must sit next to `server.js`. A `.env` inside `frontend/` is not read (and would be a leak risk).

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `PAYPAL_CLIENT_ID`, `PAYPAL_SECRET` | Sandbox REST app credentials |
| `AI_API_KEY` | Turns on the AI assistant. Free key from Google AI Studio. Blank = AI off, basic voice parser used |
| `AI_BASE_URL`, `AI_MODEL` | Optional. Defaults to Gemini's free tier; any OpenAI-compatible provider with tool calling works |
| `APP_PIN` | 4-digit PIN required for every payment (default `1234`, change it) |
| `MAX_AMOUNT` | Per-payment demo limit in USD (default 500) |
| `PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ID` | Turns on `/webhooks/paypal` (see Webhooks below). Blank = webhooks off, statuses are polled |
| `ENABLE_SIMULATOR` | `1` shows demo buttons on the dashboard that fake a webhook delivery. Demo only, leave off when deployed |
| `INVOICES_PER_MIN` | Invoice limit per IP (default 10), since each invoice sends an email |
| `PORT` | Default 3001 |

## The AI assistant

Say or type a request in your own words, for example *"pay my electricity bill and send John 20 dollars"* or *"how much did I send last week?"*. An LLM with five tools (`get_balance`, `list_payees`, `get_recent_payments`, `propose_payment`, `request_payment`) works out what you mean, asks a short question if something is missing, and prepares the payments.

**The AI can never move money.** `propose_payment` only stores a proposal on the server. The app reads every proposal back, you confirm by voice or button, and you enter your PIN. Only then does `/agent/confirm` run the payout. Proposals expire after 5 minutes, work once, and belong to the browser session that created them. Your PIN is stripped from what you say before the request reaches the model, so the model never sees it. Free AI tiers may use prompts to improve the provider's products, so only use sandbox data and never type real personal details. `/agent` is rate-limited per IP to protect your API quota.

Plain commands such as "send 5 dollars to John", "pay electricity bill" or "check balance" skip the AI and are handled instantly by the built-in parser. Anything longer or less clear (several payments, questions, follow-ups) goes to the AI. Add `?ai=always` to the page address (`http://localhost:3001/?ai=always`) to send everything to the AI, for example when recording a demo.

When a request goes to the AI it takes one model call (the app writes its own read-back). The server logs each one (`Agent: ... ms`) and the browser console (F12) shows `[InclusivePay] AI request: ... ms`, plus a warning if the browser's speech takes more than 8 seconds. Slow AI? Lower `AI_TIMEOUT_MS`, or see `AI_REASONING_EFFORT` in `.env.example`.

If the AI is unavailable, the app falls back to a simple built-in voice parser, so payments still work.

Code: `agent.js` (tools, prompt, agent loop) and the `/agent` and `/agent/confirm` routes in `server.js`.

## Dashboard (AG Grid)

Open **http://localhost:3001/dashboard.html** (or the "Open full dashboard" link on the main page).

- Two AG Grid tables: **payments you sent** and **invoices you requested**, with live totals, search, sorting, paging and CSV export.
- Custom AG Grid widgets: a status **chip** (icon plus words, never colour alone), a signed **amount** renderer (−$2.00 out, +$20.00 in), a **Read aloud / Open on PayPal** action cell, and a **status filter** component with labelled checkboxes. Press **R** on a focused row to hear it.
- Three themes (Midnight, Daylight, High contrast) and three text sizes, built by re-skinning AG Grid's alpine theme with CSS variables. Text colours are checked against WCAG AA contrast. Choices are remembered, and the default follows your OS light/dark and high-contrast settings.
- KPI tiles, a spending-by-recipient chart, and a **live activity feed** that labels where each update came from (PayPal webhook, status check, app, or simulated).

## Request money (PayPal Invoicing)

Say *"request 20 dollars from John"*, use the **Request Money** card, or ask the assistant. The app reads it back, you confirm, and it creates and sends a PayPal sandbox invoice to the contact's email. Asking for money moves nothing out of your account, so it needs your confirmation but not your PIN. Only contacts can be invoiced, not bills.

## Webhooks (live status updates)

Without webhooks the app asks PayPal for status every few seconds. With webhooks, PayPal tells the server the moment a payout or invoice changes, and the server pushes it to every open page (the dashboard row flips live, and the main page says "Payment of $2.00 to John is now SUCCESS").

1. Give your local server a public HTTPS address. Free options that need no payment: `cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:3001` (Cloudflare quick tunnel) or ngrok's free plan. A deployed app (for example on Render) already has one.
2. In developer.paypal.com open **Apps & Credentials > Sandbox > your app** and scroll to **Webhooks > Add Webhook**. URL: `https://YOUR-PUBLIC-ADDRESS/webhooks/paypal`.
3. Tick these events: `PAYMENT.PAYOUTSBATCH.PROCESSING`, `PAYMENT.PAYOUTSBATCH.SUCCESS`, `PAYMENT.PAYOUTSBATCH.DENIED`, the `PAYMENT.PAYOUTS-ITEM.*` events, `INVOICING.INVOICE.PAID`, `INVOICING.INVOICE.CANCELLED`.
4. Copy the **Webhook ID** PayPal shows into `.env` as `PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ID=...` and restart.

Every delivery is verified with PayPal's `verify-webhook-signature` API before it is believed, duplicates are ignored, and an out-of-order "processing" event can't undo a "success". If `PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ID` is not set, the endpoint refuses all requests.

**No public URL yet?** Set `ENABLE_SIMULATOR=1`. The dashboard then shows two demo buttons that make the server act as if PayPal had sent a webhook. Those feed entries are clearly labelled "Simulated", so don't present them as real deliveries.

## What you can say

- "Check my balance"
- "Send 5 dollars to John" (contacts: John, Steve)
- "Pay electricity bill" (pays the amount due; also internet, water, gas, phone)
- "Request 20 dollars from Steve" (sends a PayPal invoice, no PIN needed)
- "Read my recent payments"
- Add "PIN 1 2 3 4" to the command, or you'll be asked for it.

**Wait for the beep.** When you press Space (or the confirm and PIN prompts finish speaking) the microphone takes a moment to open. A short beep means it is open and you can speak. If nothing is understood the app listens again, and after a few tries it asks you to type instead. Use headphones when possible so the app's own voice doesn't reach the microphone.

Every payment is read back ("Send $5.00 to John") and needs a spoken or typed **confirm** before any money moves. Press **Space** anywhere to start talking. The speaker button turns spoken replies off for screen-reader users.

## Notes

- Payouts go from your sandbox business account to the recipient emails in `server.js` (`CONTACTS`). Bills go to placeholder biller addresses.
- Payment and invoice status is PayPal's own (`PENDING` → `SUCCESS`, `SENT` → `PAID`), pushed by webhooks when configured and otherwise polled.
- `transactions.json` and `invoices.json` are local demo storage (git-ignored). Use a real database for anything beyond a demo.
- Balance comes from the PayPal Server SDK (Transaction Search) when the sandbox app has that feature enabled; otherwise a mock balance that goes down as you pay.
- The PIN is a demo-grade control. A real product would use proper user authentication.
